title: Word Master Checkpoint
intro: You can measure text, reshape it, clean it up and cut pieces out of it. Eleven rounds across both lessons. Get them right on the first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.explain: .upper() turns every letter into a capital.
len() counts the characters, and "cat" has three of them. Spaces would count too.

rounds.prompt: We want lowercase but the method name is wrong. Pick the fix.
rounds.explain: The method is called .lower(). Python has no .lowercase(), so this stops with an AttributeError.

rounds.prompt: This one surprises almost everyone. What prints?
rounds.explain: A string method builds a new string and hands it back. Nothing stored it, so message never changed.
.strip() removes the spaces at each end, so what is left matches "yes" exactly. Without the strip it would be False.

rounds.prompt: What is the first letter printed?
rounds.explain: Strings are indexed like lists, and index 0 is the very first character.
A slice takes indexes 0, 1 and 2 and stops before 3. The stop number is the first letter left out.

rounds.prompt: Leaving out the first number. What prints?
rounds.explain: With no stop number the slice runs to the end, so you get everything from index 3 onwards.

rounds.prompt: Which slice gives the last two letters of any string?
rounds.explain: A negative start counts back from the end. word[-2] on its own would give only one letter, not two.

rounds.prompt: Match each tool to what it does.

pairs.right: Removes spaces at the start and end
Swaps one piece of text for another

rounds.explain: The first four measure or reshape the whole string, while the last two cut pieces out of it by index.

rounds.prompt: Store a word, then print its first three letters in capitals.
rounds.explain: Slice first to get the piece you want, then reshape that piece. Doing it the other way round works too, but this order makes each step easy to check.
